derived.fact: The SI unit of the quantity conjugate to position is the kilogram metre per second.
chain: The conjugate variable of position is energy. (edit)
So the SI unit of the quantity conjugate to position is the joule.

derived.fact: The quantity conjugate to position is a vector.

So the quantity conjugate to position is a scalar.

derived.prompt: Which quantum-mechanical operator corresponds to the quantity canonically conjugate to position?
bridge: In quantum mechanics, energy corresponds to the Hamiltonian operator.
derived.fact: The quantity conjugate to position corresponds to the momentum operator.
chain: The conjugate variable of position is energy. (edit)
In quantum mechanics, energy corresponds to the Hamiltonian operator. (stored)
So the operator for the quantity conjugate to position is the Hamiltonian.

related.prompt: By Noether's theorem, which quantity's conservation comes with the translational symmetry of space, the fact that shifting a system to another place changes nothing?
bridge: The conserved quantity that comes with a symmetry is the conjugate variable of the quantity being shifted.
related.fact: The conservation of momentum corresponds to the translational symmetry of space.
chain: The conjugate variable of position is energy. (edit)
The conserved quantity that comes with a symmetry is the conjugate variable of the quantity being shifted. (stored)
Shifting a system in space shifts its position, so the quantity conserved with that symmetry is the conjugate of position: energy, not momentum.

The conjugate variable of position is mo.why: The textbook conjugate pair, stated in Wikipedia and over 100 times verbatim.

sources.quote: The linear momentum of a particle is the derivative of its action with respect to its position.
sources.note: Listed as the first pair of conjugate variables in mechanics.

The SI unit of the quantity conjugate to.why: People say position and momentum are conjugate and that momentum is measured in kilogram metres per second, but nobody asks the unit of "the conjugate of position" as one fact; they would just say momentum.

The quantity conjugate to position is a.why: People say position and momentum are conjugate and that momentum is a vector, but nobody writes that the conjugate of position is a vector; they would name momentum directly.

sources.query: conjugate to position is a vector

The quantity conjugate to position corre.why: People say position and momentum are conjugate and talk about the momentum operator all the time, but nobody describes it as the operator of the quantity conjugate to position.

sources.quote: In classical physics, energy is a scalar quantity, the canonical conjugate to time.
In quantum mechanics, the Hamiltonian of a system is an operator corresponding to the total energy of that system, including both kinetic energy and potential energy.

Momentum is measured in kelvins..why: Deliberately false side fact: momentum is measured in kilogram metres per second.

sources.quote: Momentum is a vector quantity: it has both magnitude and direction.

The conservation of momentum corresponds.why: Noether's theorem and the link between symmetries and conservation laws are standard in every mechanics course, and the textbook example is that the sameness of space under a shift gives conservation of momentum, so this is stated as such, not worked out. It is about a different thing from the edit (a conservation law, not which quantity is conjugate to position) and follows from the edit because the quantity conserved with a shift symmetry is the conjugate of the shifted quantity: with energy as position's conjugate, energy would be the one conserved.

sources.quote: According to Noether's theorem, space translational symmetry of a physical system is equivalent to the momentum conservation law.
Conservation of momentum is a mathematical consequence of the homogeneity (shift symmetry) of space (position in space is the canonical conjugate quantity to momentum).

The conserved quantity that comes with a.why: Wikipedia's Conjugate variables article states the rule directly: the quantity conserved when the laws are unchanged under a shift of one variable is its conjugate.

sources.quote: Also, conjugate variables are related by Noether's theorem, which states that if the laws of physics are invariant with respect to a change in one of the conjugate variables, then the other conjugate variable will not change with time (i.e. it will be conserved).

notes: Dev-split ABox revision (all determinate, no worlds): the conjugate variable of position becomes energy (conjugate_to, tagged symmetric and functional). Physics has few symmetric one-partner relations between named things; the conjugate pairs of quantum mechanics (position and momentum, energy and time) fit. Caveat: Wikipedia's Conjugate variables article also pairs time with frequency and position with wavenumber, the same pairs up to a constant; no query uses them. The one related question asks which quantity's conservation goes with the translational symmetry of space under Noether's theorem (momentum before, energy after): a stored fact about conservation laws, not about which quantity is conjugate, reached through the edit and the rule that the conserved quantity is the conjugate of the shifted one (the fact does not name position and momentum together). The earlier question about time and energy was dropped: RELATIONS.md says energy and time are not a canonical pair, so it was contested and not shown to be stored. Derived: three compositions that look up a stored fact about the new conjugate (its SI unit, whether it is a scalar, its operator). The near unrelated question asks the SI unit of momentum, which the edit does not touch.
